8. Mr. Mohammad Shafiqul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-appellant submits that the accused-appellant and the complainant-respondent have entered into a compromise with the help of their relatives and friends and compromised the matter on the terms and conditions which stated in the application for compromise. The complainant-respondent also will get the 50% of the cheque amount which has been deposited by the accused-appellant earlier at the time of filing appeal. He lastly submits that since the parties have entered into a compromise and settled the dispute between them and therefore, he prayed for allowed the appeal and acquittal the accused-appellant from the charge on the basis of compromise. 

 9. Mrs. Afsana Begum, the learned Advocate appearing for the complainant-respondent has conceded the submissions of the learned Advocate for the accused-appellant and submits that he has instruction from his client that they have entered into compromise and accordingly they have submitted an application for compromise before this Court and as such she has no objection if the accused-appellant acquitted from the charge on the basis of compromise. 

 10. Mr. Swapan Kumar Das, the learned Assistant Attorney General submits that since both of the parties have entered into compromise and settled the dispute between them and therefore the State has nothing to oppose. 

 12. On close scrutiny of the records, it appears that the complainant-respondent and the accused-appellant have entered into compromise and settled the dispute between them. The parties are interested to compromise the dispute by some terms and conditions and accordingly, they have settled the matter out of Court and this compromise should be treated as very special circumstances of the case. The parties have entered into compromise with terms and conditions which as under: 

 14. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, relevant provision of law, I'm of the view that after making full amount the compromise was made between the parties by executing an agreement and the accept. It may be mentioned here that the law encourages the compromise between the parties regarding the commission of any offence with the permission of the Court since the case is pending before this Court. I've no hesitation to allow the compromise petition and as a result, this compromise shall have the effect of acquittal of the accused-appellant. 

 15. The criminal administration of justice encourages compromise of certain disputes and some of the cases can be compounded as provided under Section 345 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 16. In view of the reason given in the compromise petition of the parties that they, in the interest of both, compromised the matter. I am of the view that permission may be given for compounding they offences and acquit the accused-appellant under Section 345 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In the circumstances, I need not decide the appeal on merit but on the ground of compromise. 

 "An offence under section 323 of the Penal Code is compoundable under sub-section (1) of section 345 Cr. P.C. and an offence under section 379 of the Penal Code has now been made compoundable, with Court's permission, under sub-section (2) of section 345 Cr. P.C. by a recent amendment of law. In view of the reasons given in the joint-petition of the parties that they, in the interest of both, compromised the matter, we think that permission may be given for compounding the offences" 

 In view of the fact, I am led to hold that after making full payment of cheque amount the compromise made between the parties by executing an agreement appears to be satisfactory and consistent with the principle of modern delivery system of justice popularly known as Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR). 

 Since the offence under section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act is petty one and the dispute between the parties settled by compromise is of basically civil in nature, therefore, in the light of the decisions referred to above, I do not hesitate to accept the joint compromise petition field in both the appeals for disposing the same in terms of the said agreement" 

 18. In the result, the appeal is allowed on the basis of compromise. Accordingly, the application for compromise is disposed of.
